newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda to import U.S.-made engine in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Honda to import U.S.-made engine in 1997.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd will import its U.S. unit-made engines to Japan from autumn next year, Honda President Nobuhiko Kawamoto told a news conference on Friday.
The 3-litre V-6 engines are mostly for use in luxury cars.

The import is planned as part of Honda's broader programme to promote global car parts sourcing, he said. The imported V-6 engine is likely to be used in Honda's new models to be launched in Japan in late next year, industry sources said.

Honda also said it plans to launch five or six new models in 1997. Strong demand for Honda's Civic model will be a key factor behind an expected 26.4 percent growth in exports in 1997, Honda Executive Vice President Yoshihide Munekuni said.
Honda also plans to start selling its Japanese-made sports utility vehicle CR-V in the U.S. next year, he said.
